name: Cursor

surfaces.label: Cursor IDE and Agents Window (one Cursor.app process; many chats inside it)
cursor-agent / agent CLI (bundled node running index.js)
Cloud / background agents (run on Cursor VMs; nothing local to match)

working_signals.meaning: IDE and Agents Window: Cursor takes a wakelock when a local chat turn starts (reason agent-loop) and drops it at generation-ended. It is also dropped while the chat waits for approval (user-approval-requested) and retaken on resume (agent-loop-resumed). App-wide, not per chat. Verified from bundled source and Cursor's own log lines; the pmset assertion itself was not observed because no turn was running. Not taken for cloud agents. The CLI does not take one. Matched by owner pid only; the assertion name is not known as pmset prints it.
CLI only, UNVERIFIED: ~/.cursor/chats/<md5(cwd)>/<chat id>/store.db is written as the turn progresses. Not tested, no CLI session was run.

Weak fallback, inferred, floor unmeasured. Idle Cursor.app tree measured 0.5-1.0 percent (2026-09-29), but typing or scrolling in the IDE burns CPU, and the tree includes the integrated terminal (Terminal pty-host is a child of the main process), so a build or another agent run there can false-positive. Reasonable only for the CLI.

waiting_signals.meaning: IDE: this chat is blocked on the human (tool approval or question). Ends with reason="agent-loop-resumed". Seen in real logs from 2026-06-09. Per chat, unlike the app-wide assertion. Undocumented.
IDE: true while the chat has a pending approval. Key exists in headers and drives the wakelock release. Whether it is flushed to disk live was not checked. Undocumented, and the file is about 1.2 GB.

Fires just before a command or MCP call runs and may answer permission ask. This is a decision point, not a Notification. Cursor has NO Notification or idle-waiting event, and the Claude Code Notification hook is not mapped.

hooks.config: ~/.cursor/hooks.json (user), <project>/.cursor/hooks.json (project), /Library/Application Support/Cursor/hooks.json (enterprise, macOS), team hooks from the web dashboard. Also reads Claude Code hook configs. Not present on this Mac.

telemetry.how: No local OTLP exporter. OpenTelemetry Export is Enterprise-only, server-side (Cursor's egress IPs push OTLP/HTTP protobuf metrics and logs to a team collector; no traces). Conversation content covers Cloud Agents and Grok Bot only, not IDE or CLI. Nothing a local monitor can read. The OTEL_* strings in the CLI bundle are the OpenTelemetry JS library, not a Cursor feature.

sources.claim: CLI is a bash launcher that execs a bundled node on index.js, so the running process is named node under ~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/<version>/
sources.evidence: ~/.local/bin/cursor-agent is a symlink to ~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/2025.12.17-996666f/cursor-agent (bash script ending: exec "$NODE_BIN" --use-system-ca "$SCRIPT_DIR/index.js" "$@"); the version dir holds node, rg, spawn-helper, index.js; `cursor-agent --version` printed 2025.12.17-996666f. No CLI session was running, so the exact ps line was not observed. Re-run 2026-09-29: while `cursor-agent --version` was running, ps showed exactly `<home>/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/2025.12.17-996666f/node --use-system-ca <same dir>/index.js --version`, so exe is the versioned node path and argv holds the flags. A real interactive session's ps line is still unobserved.

sources.claim: Current docs call the CLI `agent` (curl https://cursor.com/install); this Mac has the older cursor-agent name. Docs show resume forms `agent ls`, `agent resume`, `agent --continue`, `agent --resume="chat-id"`

sources.claim: The CLI never takes a power assertion or spawns caffeinate
sources.evidence: grep -l -iE 'caffeinate|IOPMAssertion|powerSaveBlocker' over every *.js in ~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/2025.12.17-996666f/ printed nothing. Only checked in this one old version.

sources.claim: IDE agent holds an Electron wakelock exactly while a local chat turn runs and releases it while waiting for approval
sources.evidence: /Applications/Cursor.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js, class ComposerWakelockManager (out-build/vs/workbench/contrib/composer/browser/composerWakelockManager.js): constructor calls _acquire('agent-loop') unless composerHandle.data.hasBlockingPendingActions; a reactive watch calls _release('user-approval-requested') when it turns true and _acquire('agent-loop-resumed') when it turns false. It is built in submitChat only when !createdFromBackgroundAgent.bcId. out/main.js powerMainService.startWakelockForOwner calls powerSaveBlocker.start('prevent-app-suspension').

sources.claim: Those wakelocks really fire on real turns, 10 starts with reason agent-loop and 1 with agent-loop-resumed, each release logged as generation-ended or user-approval-requested
sources.evidence: grep over ~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/logs/20260609T181642/{main.log,window*/renderer.log} counted: '[ComposerWakelockManager] Acquired wakelock reason="agent-loop"' x10, 'reason="agent-loop-resumed"' x1, 'Released wakelock reason="generation-ended"' x10, 'reason="user-approval-requested"' x1. main.log line: '[PowerMainService] Started wakelock id=0 owner=window:1 reason="agent-loop" activeCount=1'. Later log sessions (2026-07-24, 2026-09-29) hold no such lines.

sources.claim: `cursor <path>` (the shell command installed from the IDE) starts a short-lived process whose executable is the IDE binary itself, so it matches the ide process spec without being the IDE
sources.evidence: /Applications/Cursor.app/Contents/Resources/app/bin/cursor: find_cursor_cli sets ELECTRON="$CONTENTS/MacOS/Cursor" and CLI="$CONTENTS/Resources/app/out/cli.js", and use_cursor_cli runs ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$ELECTRON" "$CLI" "$@". Its parent is the user's shell, so the probe's outermost-process rule does not drop it. Fix: exclude_args holds the cli.js path (exact-token match, so it covers only /Applications installs). Not run live, to avoid opening the app; ps shows no such process now.

sources.claim: Non-session CLI subcommands are NOT excluded: only -v/--version and -h/--help are in exclude_args, so login, logout, mcp, status, whoami, update, upgrade, create-chat, ls, resume, help and install-shell-integration would show as brief idle CLI sessions
sources.evidence: cursor-agent --help lists them. Not added to exclude_args because the probe matches exact argv tokens anywhere, so an unquoted prompt containing 'login' or 'status' would hide a real session. Trade-off left open.

sources.claim: power_assertion.name is matched as a substring of the name pmset prints; prose there never matches
sources.evidence: completeness critic of wave 3 checked tools/agents_probe.py against the six rows; name set from the row's own cited source or removed

notes: Cursor is one Electron process for all local chats, so the process is the wrong unit: one Cursor.app can hold many chats and the Agents Window is just another window in it. Per-chat state needs Cursor's log lines or hooks. The best cheap live signal is the app-wide wakelock (drops while any chat waits for approval, so with two chats a wait can be masked by the other still running). The CLI is a separate node process with no power assertion and no per-turn child marker known. Cloud agents have no local footprint. Confidence is documented, not verified-locally, because no agent turn was running to watch the assertion or the CLI process live. Verification 2026-09-29: the IDE process spec also matched the short-lived `cursor <path>` launcher (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE running out/cli.js); fixed with exclude_args. tree_cpu floor 10 is not measured against a real turn, and the IDE tree includes integrated-terminal children (pty-host), so a build or another agent running in Cursor's terminal can mark the IDE working; treat it as a last resort.
